caseStudies.title: Panel visibility across shop and site
caseStudies.summary: Replaced spreadsheet status with a shared panel tracker the whole project could trust.
caseStudies.problem: A curtain wall fabricator tracked panel progress in multiple spreadsheets. Site teams called daily for updates; planners spent evenings reconciling versions.
caseStudies.built: A web app for panel lifecycle status, simple filters by zone and elevation, and roles for shop, logistics, and site — fed by the team’s existing IDs.
caseStudies.result: Fewer status calls, one agreed view of progress, and faster handoffs when units left the factory.

quote.text: We finally stopped arguing about which file was current.
quote.author: Operations lead (placeholder)

caseStudies.title: Drawing review without the chase
caseStudies.summary: Centralized DWG review so comments and revisions lived in one place.
caseStudies.problem: Review cycles lived in email. Markups got lost; newcomers couldn’t see why a detail changed.
caseStudies.built: A viewer-led workflow with comment threads tied to drawings, notification digests, and a clear “current set” for each package.
caseStudies.result: Shorter review loops and a trail new team members could follow without a meeting.

quote.text: The current set is obvious now — that alone was worth it.
quote.author: Project engineer (placeholder)

caseStudies.title: Field reporting that people finish
caseStudies.summary: A light mobile-friendly log that cut end-of-day admin without adding process weight.
caseStudies.problem: Daily reports were incomplete or late because forms felt like punishment after a long shift.
caseStudies.built: A short guided form, photo attach, and auto summary for managers — designed with site supervisors, not for them.
caseStudies.result: Higher completion rates and managers who could skim mornings instead of chasing evenings.

quote.text: It’s short enough that people actually do it.
quote.author: Site manager (placeholder)
